findings.title: PowerShell Command Injection & Improper Quote Escaping in Offline TTS
findings.evidence: Line 35 uses safe_text = text.replace("'", "''").replace('"', '`"') inside a single-quoted PowerShell string, while abs_out (line 41), rate (line 39), and volume (line 40) are interpolated directly into ps_cmd passed to powershell -Command without escaping or int validation.
findings.current_behavior: An output path containing a single quote (e.g. O'Brien_vo.wav) breaks out of the PowerShell string literal and executes arbitrary PowerShell tokens; backtick-escaped double quotes inside single quotes are spoken literally.
findings.expected_behavior: All arguments (text, output path, rate, volume) should be passed via safe script parameters (-File with param block) or stdin/environment variables with strict integer range validation.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Command injection risk on untrusted filenames/script inputs and corrupted narration speech when narration text contains double quotes.
findings.reproduction_steps: Call generate_voiceover('Say "hello"', "outputs/test';whoami;'.wav").
findings.recommended_solution: Create a parameterized PowerShell helper script (like scripts/win_ocr.ps1) accepting [string]$Text, [string]$OutPath, [int]$Rate, [int]$Volume via subprocess argument list (never string interpolation into -Command).
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; verify Phase 1 Test B and Phase 3 Test 08 still produce identical WAV output.

findings.title: Campaign Lifecycle State Machine Gatekeeper Bypass
findings.evidence: Docstring L142 states QC_APPROVED requires technical QC passed and creative QC >= 72, but L163 only checks ['READY_TO_PUBLISH', 'PUBLISHED']. L159-160 compute current_idx and target_idx and never enforce sequential transitions. Live DB confirms multiplatform-pack-01 and BPB_DAY_05 have status='QC_APPROVED' with technical_qc_passed=0 and creative_qc_score=0. update_status() allows setting status='PUBLISHED' directly without human approval.
findings.current_behavior: Items can skip straight from IDEA to QC_APPROVED with 0/90 QC, and update_status() bypasses the Zero-Unauthorized-Publishing check.
findings.expected_behavior: QC_APPROVED must enforce technical_qc_passed == 1 and creative_qc_score >= 72 (or Phase 5 QC PASS/approved override); sequential transitions must be enforced; update_status() must reject direct PUBLISHED transitions.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Weakens governance over publishing readiness and contradicts the studio's mandatory QC gate.
findings.reproduction_steps: Inspect data/campaign_tracker.sqlite rows multiplatform-pack-01 and BPB_DAY_05, or call update_status('BPB_DAY_05', 'PUBLISHED').
findings.recommended_solution: Include 'QC_APPROVED' in the QC gate check in advance_state(), enforce valid transition map, restrict update_status() from setting PUBLISHED/READY_TO_PUBLISH without gate checks, and align with Phase 5 qc_orchestrator approval records.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Medium; scripts/run_test_e_lifecycle.py and existing CLI workflows calling update_status() must be verified.

findings.title: Cross-Project Brand Hashtag Leakage in Global Export Profiles
findings.evidence: export_profiles.json defines default_hashtags: ['#BlockPuzzle', '#PyapirasGames', '#Reels'] globally on instagram_reels (and #PyapirasGames on all 4 profiles). multi_platform_exporter.py:L759 copies eff_spec.get('default_hashtags', []) verbatim into every project's delivery_record JSON. platform_adapter.py hardcodes #BlockPuzzle #PyapirasGames across all captions.
findings.current_behavior: Any shared-artifact export for Expand eziSales (B2B ERP) or future non-game projects receives #BlockPuzzle and #PyapirasGames in its staged platform delivery record.
findings.expected_behavior: Global platform export profiles must contain zero project-specific brand hashtags; default hashtags must be sourced exclusively from projects/<project>/knowledge/ or project-specific configuration.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Direct violation of project brand isolation; risks publishing enterprise ERP tutorials tagged with #BlockPuzzle.
findings.reproduction_steps: Run multi_platform_exporter.py --project expand-ezisales and inspect deliveries/instagram_reels_delivery.json -> caption_and_hashtags.hashtags.
findings.recommended_solution: Remove #BlockPuzzle and #PyapirasGames from config/production/export_profiles.json; load project hashtags from per-project profile config with empty fallback.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; Phase 4 tests check delivery record structure, not hardcoded BlockPuzzle hashtags.

findings.title: Unsanitized Path Traversal & Missing QC Gate in Google Drive Sync
findings.evidence: GDRIVE_ROOT is hardcoded to r'G:\My Drive\Vids\generated'. Line 55 builds dest_folder = os.path.join(GDRIVE_ROOT, content_id) without validating content_id against '..' or absolute path injection. Lines 58-67 copy videos without checking qc_report.json or human approval state.
findings.current_behavior: Passing --content-id '..\..\arbitrary' writes outside GDRIVE_ROOT; unapproved or FAIL-status renders can be synced directly to the phone-connected Drive folder.
findings.expected_behavior: Validate content_id strictly (slug regex), resolve and assert dest_folder stays inside GDRIVE_ROOT, read GDRIVE_ROOT from env/config, and require verified READY_TO_PUBLISH approval (unless explicit --allow-unapproved flag).
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Local path traversal risk inside synced Google Drive storage and accidental distribution of QC-failed videos to mobile devices.
findings.reproduction_steps: Inspect scripts/drive_sync.py:L14 and L55-67; invoke with a FAIL-status content_id or traversal string.
findings.recommended_solution: Add strict slug validation + os.path.commonpath containment check, move GDRIVE_ROOT to env/config, check Phase 5 QC approval gate before copying, and add unit tests.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; existing manual sync workflows will need either an approved QC job or explicit --force-preview flag.

findings.title: Hardcoded Absolute Local Paths Persisted in SQLite and Job JSON Records
findings.evidence: Audit found 12 JSON files in data/ (totalling 291 occurrences) and 3 SQLite rows (day-04-offline-proof, ezisales-tut-01-order-booking, multiplatform-pack-01) persisting 'C:\Users\Dell\Downloads\video gen\...'.
findings.current_behavior: Renaming the local root folder to 'Social Media Video Production Studio' or cloning to another workstation invalidates stored paths in historical job, export, QC, and campaign records.
findings.expected_behavior: All persisted paths inside data/ JSON files and SQLite should be stored relative to WORKSPACE_ROOT using POSIX forward slashes and resolved dynamically at runtime.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Breaks audit traceability, qc_orchestrator compare/status path lookups, and portability across machines or after folder rename.
findings.reproduction_steps: Inspect data/campaign_tracker.sqlite output_location column and data/export_jobs/*.json master_path fields.
findings.recommended_solution: Add a shared path_utils.to_workspace_relative() / resolve_workspace_path() helper, migrate existing JSON/SQLite paths cleanly during remediation, and enforce relative persistence going forward.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Medium; tests asserting os.path.exists(job['output_file']) must resolve relative paths against WORKSPACE_ROOT.

findings.expected_behavior: All automated tests must isolate SQLite DBs, output directories, qc_jobs/, and approval audit logs inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() via dependency injection or environment overrides.

findings.title: FFmpeg '-t' Option Placement & Fragile Overlay Filtergraph String Parsing
findings.evidence: Line 95 places ['-t', str(duration)] after '-i abs_in' and directly before extra_inputs (PNG overlays), meaning FFmpeg interprets -t as an input option for the first overlay PNG rather than the source video (masked only because -t is repeated as an output option on line 132). Line 107 assumes audio_input_idx = 1 + (len(extra_inputs) // 2), which breaks if any extra input adds a flag like -loop 1. Lines 76-78 parse filter strings with brittle .split('[ov')[1].split(']overlay=')[1].
findings.current_behavior: Works only for static single-flag PNG overlay inputs because output -t masks input -t misplacement; fails immediately if multi-flag overlay inputs (e.g. animated GIF/WebM or -loop 1) are added.
findings.expected_behavior: Place -t cleanly as an output option (or input option before -i abs_in), track input_count explicitly as an integer counter, and pass structured overlay specs instead of re-parsing FFmpeg filter strings.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Latent pipeline failure when extending overlay support to animated badges, logos, or multi-flag FFmpeg inputs.
findings.reproduction_steps: Add '-loop', '1' to an overlay input in overlay_engine.py and invoke VideoProcessor.normalize_and_trim_scene(); audio_input_idx computes wrong stream index.
findings.recommended_solution: Remove duplicate misplaced -t at L95, track next_input_idx explicitly, and have OverlayEngine return structured dicts rather than strings parsed with split().
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; covered by Phase 3 tests 05-07 and 12-13.

findings.title: Aspect-Ratio Distortion in Fallback Branch of FFmpeg Batch Utility
findings.evidence: Line 36 (system FFmpeg) uses scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1080:1920:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black, whereas line 39 (Remotion FFmpeg fallback) runs bare -vf "scale=1080:1920".
findings.current_behavior: On machines without system ffmpeg on PATH (like this workspace), trim_and_scale.bat stretches any non-9:16 video to 1080x1920 without letterboxing.
findings.expected_behavior: Both branches must apply identical aspect-ratio-preserving scale + pad filtergraph.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Distorts gameplay grids or ERP screens whenever operators use the legacy batch helper script.
findings.reproduction_steps: Run renderers\ffmpeg\trim_and_scale.bat on a 16:9 clip without system ffmpeg on PATH.
findings.recommended_solution: Update line 39 filtergraph to match line 36 verbatim.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Negligible.

findings.title: Missing Offline ASR Engine & Automated Subjective Creative Evaluator
findings.evidence: No local ASR package (faster-whisper / whisper) is installed; every video with audio triggers AUD_007 (REVIEW_REQUIRED, confidence=0.0). Creative dimensions Story Clarity and Audience Relevance always require manual human review.
findings.current_behavior: Honest fail-safe: surfaces REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than faking PASS, but prevents fully automated transcript-to-script verification.
findings.expected_behavior: Optional local offline faster-whisper integration for automated voiceover transcript alignment (still preserving mandatory human final approval).
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Increases human listen-through time as video volume scales.
findings.reproduction_steps: Run qc_orchestrator.py run-master on day-04-no-wifi-revision.mp4 and inspect AUD_007 in qc_summary.md.
findings.recommended_solution: Add optional faster-whisper backend in audio_qc.py with graceful fallback to AUD_007 when not installed.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Medium; adds ~150MB-500MB local model weights and CPU runtime overhead.

findings.title: Fragmented Platform Profile Schemas & Dual Legacy/Modern Engines
findings.affected_function_or_component: Profile resolution & Phase 1 vs Phase 4/5 engine overlap
findings.evidence: Four overlapping profile config sources define platform specs using inconsistent singular vs plural slugs (instagram_reel vs instagram_reels, youtube_short vs youtube_shorts). Phase 1 scripts (creative_qc.py with static 80/90 scores, qc_verifier.py, platform_adapter.py) coexist alongside Phase 4/5 replacements (multi_platform_exporter.py, qc_orchestrator.py).
findings.current_behavior: Developers must reconcile multiple config schemas and risk accidentally invoking legacy static-score QC instead of Phase 5 automated QC.
findings.expected_behavior: Single canonical platform/render profile registry with explicit aliases and clear deprecation wrappers on Phase 1 legacy helpers.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Configuration drift, mismatched platform keys across DB/manifests/exports, and elevated maintenance overhead.
findings.reproduction_steps: Compare profile IDs in config/platform_presets/ vs config/production/video_profiles.json vs config/production/export_profiles.json.
findings.recommended_solution: Consolidate profile definitions behind a single config loader with normalized slug aliases and mark Phase 1 legacy scripts clearly as compatibility shims.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Medium; requires updating Phase 1-3 scripts to share the normalized loader.

findings.title: Unbounded Subprocess Executions Missing Timeout Safeguards Across 15 Scripts
findings.evidence: AST audit identified 25 subprocess.run() calls in scripts/ lacking a timeout parameter (including FFmpeg renders, ffprobe calls, PowerShell SAPI5 TTS, and sub-script orchestrations).
findings.current_behavior: A malformed media stream causing FFmpeg or PowerShell to stall will hang the pipeline or batch job indefinitely.
findings.expected_behavior: All subprocess calls should specify bounded timeouts (e.g. 30s for ffprobe/OCR, 300s-600s for FFmpeg renders) and catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired cleanly.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Risk of silent hung automation jobs and leaked background FFmpeg processes.
findings.reproduction_steps: AST inspect subprocess.run calls in scripts/media_engine.py:L71, scripts/audio_qc.py:L43, scripts/multi_platform_exporter.py:L387.
findings.recommended_solution: Centralize subprocess execution in a shared helper with configurable default timeouts and structured TimeoutExpired error reporting.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; ensure generous timeout for long 16:9 YouTube tutorial renders.

findings.title: Non-Atomic JSON Persistence & Missing SQLite Concurrency Safeguards
findings.evidence: All JSON catalog and job state saves write directly with open(path, 'w') without temp-file + os.replace() atomic swap. campaign_manager.py connects to SQLite with default timeout and journal mode (no WAL mode or explicit busy_timeout).
findings.current_behavior: An interrupted process mid-write can truncate data/media_catalog.json or data/audio_catalog.json to 0 bytes; concurrent CLI runs risk sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked.
findings.expected_behavior: Write JSON files atomically (write to .tmp in same directory, flush/fsync, os.replace) and enable SQLite PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Potential catalog corruption or lock failures under concurrent production/QC runs.
findings.reproduction_steps: Code inspection of JSON write blocks across scripts/ and get_db_connection() in scripts/campaign_manager.py:L30-34.
findings.recommended_solution: Introduce atomic_write_json() utility and configure SQLite WAL mode + busy_timeout in get_db_connection().
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: Low; WAL creates -wal/-shm sidecar files (add *.sqlite-wal / *.sqlite-shm to .gitignore).

findings.title: Missing Secret-File Protections in .gitignore & Unpinned Python Dependencies
findings.evidence: .gitignore lacks entries for .env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key, credentials.json, token.json, *.sqlite-wal. Workspace has no requirements.txt or dependency pins inside pyproject.toml despite requiring Pillow (13.0.0), numpy (2.4.2), and imageio-ffmpeg (0.8.1).
findings.current_behavior: Future API credentials placed in .env or credentials.json risk accidental Git commits; fresh machine setup has no reproducible pip install manifest.
findings.expected_behavior: Add comprehensive secret ignore rules to .gitignore and declare pinned/bounded dependencies in pyproject.toml and requirements.txt.
findings.business_or_technical_impact: Elevated risk of future credential leakage to GitHub and non-reproducible Python setups.
findings.reproduction_steps: Inspect .gitignore and verify absence of requirements.txt.
findings.recommended_solution: Extend .gitignore with secret/env patterns and add dependencies = ['pillow>=10,<14', 'numpy>=1.26,<3', 'imageio-ffmpeg>=0.5,<1'] to pyproject.toml plus requirements.txt.
findings.potential_risks_of_fixing: None.

findings.title: 224.58 MB of Reclaimable Exact Duplicate Binary Files Across Workspace
